requirements.requirement: opsbot account created on node1 and node2
requirements.summary: id opsbot confirms uid=1000(opsbot) exists on both nodes, created via useradd -m.

requirements.requirement: opsbot on node1 has SSH key-based access to run commands as opsbot on node2
requirements.summary: ed25519 keypair generated for opsbot on node1, public key installed into node2's opsbot authorized_keys (600 perms), and a live SSH session from opsbot@node1 to opsbot@node2 executed commands (SSH_KEY_AUTH_OK, whoami=opsbot, hostname=node2), later reconfirmed post-restart and in a final end-to-end check.

requirements.requirement: Key-based authentication required for opsbot on both systems (password auth rejected)
requirements.summary: Password logins were locked via passwd -l on both nodes (shadow shows '!'), and a Match User opsbot sshd block enforcing PubkeyAuthentication yes / PasswordAuthentication no / AuthenticationMethods publickey was applied and validated (sshd -t, sshd -T -C user=opsbot) on both nodes. Forced password-only SSH attempts to node2 and to node1 itself were both rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)'.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — opsbot account creation on both nodes, working SSH key-based access from opsbot@node1 to opsbot@node2, and enforced key-only authentication for opsbot on both systems — are directly and consistently evidenced by command output, including explicit rejection of password-based attempts and successful key-based command execution. The independent node-restart protocol was also completed for both nodes with pre-restart boot-identity/healthy-state capture, restart acknowledgement, differing post-restart boot IDs cross-checked against the fixed after-executor snapshots, and full re-verification of the opsbot configuration and cross-node SSH after each reboot.
limitations: The /etc/hosts append on node1 (cmd-40ffd3b40c2b4e41) has no clearly demonstrated purpose relative to the task or its verification steps, since IP resolution for SSH tests used $CLUSTER_HOSTS directly; its actual necessity could not be confirmed from the available evidence.
Pre-existing baseline /etc/hosts content on node1 prior to cmd-40ffd3b40c2b4e41 was not captured, so it cannot be confirmed whether the appended lines were duplicates of existing entries.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor's actions were tightly scoped to the opsbot task: user creation, keypair generation, authorized_keys install, password locking, and an sshd Match-User drop-in, all validated with sshd -t before reload. One early keygen attempt (cmd-bc619becf3864c93) failed due to file ownership order and was corrected in cmd-7a35d2812eb440d4 with no lasting residue. An SSH probe to the wrong target (cmd-2ec4106b5ab8480c) failed harmlessly and was superseded by the correct node2 probe. The one mutation without a clear tie to the opsbot task is cmd-40ffd3b40c2b4e41, which appended CLUSTER_HOSTS entries to /etc/hosts on node1; this is a low-risk, non-destructive change but subsequent SSH commands resolved node2's IP directly from $CLUSTER_HOSTS rather than /etc/hosts, so the edit had no demonstrated necessity for the task or its verification. Post-restart, the temporary-file and listening-socket deltas between after-prepare and after-executor snapshots (new systemd-private dirs, /tmp/reboot.log, new sshd/chronyd PIDs) are expected artifacts of the reboot process itself, not executor residue, and no failed services or package-health issues appear in the after-executor snapshot on either node.
